newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA TO IMPORT NATURAL GAS LIQUIDS FOR POWER.
newsitem.headline: INDIA TO IMPORT NATURAL GAS LIQUIDS FOR POWER.

text.p: India plans to import natural gas liquids (NGL) as a fuel for power generation, a petroleum ministry official said on Tuesday.
"We plan to import up to 10 million tonnes of NGL to bridge the deficit in naphtha supply," Devi Dayal, a senior civil servant in the Petroleum Ministry, told Reuters.
"The state-run Indian Oil Corp has been asked to firm up details on global availability and ruling price," he said.
Imported NGL will be supplied as an alternate fuel for naphtha-based power plants being set up in the private sector.
Companies setting up power projects on naphtha have been told to design their plants for multi-fuel operation, Dayal said.
In November 1995, the Indian government allowed setting up of short gestation liquid fuel-based power plants to bridge the gap in power supply.

Fearing a shortage of naphtha, the government restricted fuel linkages for a power generation capacity of 12,000 megawatts. "Global trends indicate that naphtha will be in short supply till the year 2005," Dayal said.
He said NGL imports were being tied up to bridge the projected shortfall in naphtha. "Moreover, preliminary figures indicate availability of NGL at prices 10 percent lower than naphtha."

Earlier, addressing a meeting organised by the Independent Power Producers Association of India (IPPAI), Dayal said oil companies will guarantee supply of liquid fuel for 80 percent plant capacity utilisation.
The proposed fuel supply guarantee will provide for compensation from oil companies to the power producers if they fail to supply the committed quantities, he said.
The IPPAI, an association of 30 companies, has been demanding such a fuel supply guarantee.
Dayal said the clause will mitigate financial risk of the power producers and ensure loans from financial institutions for their projects.

"If the power projects are unable to meet the specified capacity utilisation due to a shortfall in fuel supply, the oil companies will provide financial cover through lump sum payment or instalments to the financial institutions," he added.
